partners.mechanism_chain: GGCX (HGNC:4247) —DISRUPTS→ Vitamin K metabolism and gamma-carboxylation (REACT:R-HSA-70171); Vitamin K metabolism and gamma-carboxylation (REACT:R-HSA-70171) —DECREASES→ Reduced gamma-carboxyglutamate residues on clotting factors; Reduced gamma-carboxyglutamate residues on clotting factors —LEADS_TO→ Combined deficiency of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors (MONDO:0010187); Reduced gamma-carboxyglutamate residues on clotting factors —LEADS_TO→ Body skin hyperlaxity (MONDO:0012570); Combined deficiency of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors (MONDO:0010187) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding tendency (HP:0001929); Body skin hyperlaxity (MONDO:0012570) —LEADS_TO→ Joint hypermobility (HP:0001382). Loss-of-function mutations in GGCX impair the vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation pathway, leading to reduced levels of functional vitamin K-dependent clotting factors. This deficiency directly causes combined clotting factor deficiencies (Disease A). The altered extracellular matrix properties due to impaired carboxylation of proteins like osteocalcin and matrix Gla protein contribute to connective tissue abnormalities, including skin hyperlaxity (Disease B).

partners.diseaseBName: thrombophilia due to protein S deficiency, autosomal dominant
partners.mechanism_chain: GGCX (HGNC:4274) —DISRUPTS→ Vitamin K cycle (REACT:R-HSA-2030767); Vitamin K cycle (REACT:R-HSA-2030767) —DECREASES→ Vitamin K epoxide (CHEBI:17246); Vitamin K epoxide (CHEBI:17246) —LEADS_TO→ Vitamin K quinone (CHEBI:17247); Vitamin K quinone (CHEBI:17247) —DECREASES→ Reduced Vitamin K (CHEBI:17248); Reduced Vitamin K (CHEBI:17248) —DECREASES→ Carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent proteins (GO:0006459); Carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent proteins (GO:0006459) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding tendency (HP:0001892); PROS1 (HGNC:9812) —DISRUPTS→ Coagulation cascade (GO:0007596); Coagulation cascade (GO:0007596) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombophilia (HP:0001945). Mutations in GGCX impair the vitamin K cycle, leading to reduced carboxylation of clotting factors and thus bleeding tendency (Disease A). Separately, mutations in PROS1 disrupt the coagulation cascade by impairing Protein S function, leading to thrombophilia (Disease B). The shared mechanism lies in the convergence on the coagulation cascade, where deficient vitamin K-dependent factors (due to GGCX) and deficient Protein S (due to PROS1) both contribute to dysregulation of thrombin generation, albeit with opposing clinical manifestations.

partners.diseaseBName: thrombophilia due to protein C deficiency, autosomal recessive
partners.mechanism_chain: GGCX (HGNC:4174) —DISRUPTS→ Vitamin K metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-170481); Vitamin K metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-170481) —DISRUPTS→ Vitamin K epoxide (CHEBI:36708); Vitamin K epoxide (CHEBI:36708) —DECREASES→ Reduced Vitamin K (CHEBI:17908); Reduced Vitamin K (CHEBI:17908) —DISRUPTS→ Gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors (GO:0006389); Gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors (GO:0006389) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding tendency (HP:0001892); PROC (HGNC:9199) —DISRUPTS→ Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-569045); Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-569045) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombophilia (HP:0001655); Gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors (GO:0006389) —DECREASES→ Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-569045).
